81_marg1508: Gaius, having received the faith of Christ, good in his deeds, used to receive the preachers and hearers of the word of God, and ministered to them from his means, as is made clear in the epistle. He commends hospitality, and urges him not to give it up through the example and prompting of Diotrephes; for Diotrephes asserted that hospitality was useless. Gaius seems to have been a Corinthian, whence Paul: “I give thanks to my Lord, that I baptized none of you but Crispus and Caius.” And elsewhere: “Caius, my host, and of the whole church, saluteth you.”

Diotrephes, the heresiarch of that time, by teaching new things usurped the first place for himself.
